claims.head: Strength vs. strength
claims.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

claims.head: The Oilers want McDavid away from the big guns
claims.call: The Oilers’ L2 (Dach, McDavid and Hyman) spends at least 24% of its 5-on-5 time against the Golden Knights’ fourth line, against about 15% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending McDavid’s line (Dach, McDavid and Hyman) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Golden Knights’ fourth line is Bowman, Dowd and Gatcomb.

notes.text: Noah Hanifin is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan. That pair has had 65% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 58:59 together, up from 43% with Hanifin.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is day to day and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 49% of the team’s power-play time in 24 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, down from 30% last season.

stakes: The Golden Knights go in second in the Pacific with 31 points, 6 points behind the Oilers, first.

EDM.head: The Oilers start a half-step behind
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and gets Hanifin back. The Oilers’ best way to tip it is keeping shots to a minimum.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights start a half-step ahead
VGK.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and gets Hanifin back. Still, it’s close: the Oilers can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: The Golden Knights need a win
paras: The Oilers (17-4-3) lost 3-1 to Tampa Bay on Thursday, and the Golden Knights are winless in four (0-1-3). This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Knights second (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Oilers first (second). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Golden Knights’ record (.646) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.771) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.560), largely thanks to their finishing.
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 79-68, but only 49-46 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 24-16.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd). They also have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd), and the Oilers’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st). Edmonton has scored 3.83 goals a game, the third most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Oilers (3rd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Jack Eichel (9 G / 20 A / 29 P in 24 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL. Mark Stone (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 24 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, with five goals in eight games against Edmonton since 2023-24. Connor McDavid (13 G / 42 A / 55 P in 24 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (21 G / 23 A / 44 P in 24 GP) has a team-high 21 goals, tied for the most in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games.

Adin Hill (7-2-3 / .898 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for Vegas. Edmonton has two options in net: Devon Levi (10-2-0 / .902 SV% in 12 GS) and Tristan Jarry (6-1-3 / .909 SV% in 10 GS). Levi has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Dach, McDavid and Hyman out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Bowman, Dowd and Gatcomb.
